origin: Own exact generalized-moment uncertainty problem for a normalized real scientific signalX. X is a random variable with unknown probability law, not a hidden finite histogram or a supplied sample dataset. Five calibrated polynomial readouts are exact expectation constraints. They do not stipulate a uniform density, smoothness, finite atom count, symmetry of the probability law, a parametric family or a stochastic sampling error model.
support: For every bounded-law question the ONLY support knowledge isX in closed[-1,1], permitting arbitrary atoms at interior and endpoints. One separate explicitly unrestricted comparison permitsX anywhere on the entire real line with finite fourth moment. Do not transfer an extremizer between these two admissible sets without checking its support. All total mass is1 and no signed probability measure is allowed.
input_interpretation: Each CSV row lists coefficients of one known polynomialK_i(x)=constant+x_column*x+x2_column*x^2+x3_column*x^3+x4_column*x^4, plus its exact expected_readoutE[K_i(X)]. Reconstructm_j=E[X^j],j=0..4 in this order using the actual complete readout system. Retain actual MatrixSVD of the5x5 source coefficient matrix and actual SolveLinearSystem of the complete system, and audit every source expectation/normalization. The columns labelledx,x2,etc are polynomial coefficients, not individual measured signal values. A readout string such as1/3 denotes its exact rational value, not a truncated decimal; preserve that exact constraint in all algebraic certificates.
atom_questions: Over all admissible bounded laws, find the exact maximum possible P(X=0) and the exact maximum possible P(X=1/2). For each return a complete extremizing law as ascending distinct atom locations and aligned positive weights. Separately find the maximum P(X=1/2) over all unrestricted real-line laws with these same moments and return its complete ascending extremizing law. Decide whether this unrestricted extremizer is admissible under the original support bound and whether each extremizer is unique for its own stated problem. These are point masses, not density heights or masses in a numerical neighborhood. Prove each sharp upper bound globally with an appropriate nonnegative-polynomial/semidefinite-moment certificate and an actual feasible moment-matching extremizer; a fitted grid LP alone is insufficient.
moment_geometry: Build the3x3moment matrixM_ij=m_(i+j),i,j=0,1,2 and2x2support localizerL_ij=m_(i+j)-m_(i+j+2),i,j=0,1. Derive why the latter is positive semidefinite for bounded laws and need not be for unrestricted laws. Retain actual SymmetricEigenDecomposition and MatrixInverse for BOTH actual matrices, then use their returned inverses in point-mass bound/certificate construction. Reconcile whichever matrix or polynomial constraint is active at each queried location. All rank-one subtraction, global polynomial nonnegativity and complementarity/support claims must be checked rather than assuming a raw moment-matrix bound is sharp with bounded support.
event_boundaries: Find the sharp infimum and supremum of BOTH P(X>=0) andP(X>0) over bounded laws with the source moments. Report separately whether EACH bound is attained. Atoms exactly atzero count only in the first event. Prove global bounds with complete degree<=4polynomial majorant/minorant certificates valid on the entire bounded support; a finite mesh is not a proof. Explain equality-support restrictions and why an endpoint may be a supremum/infimum without an attaining law. When needed exhibit a genuine positive moment-matching family approaching the bound, rather than shifting an atom while leaving the other moments uncorrected.
canonical_approach_examples: As an explicit check on any nonattainment construction, construct the3atom quadrature laws matchingm0..m4 whose middle node is prescribed exactlyt=-0.01 andt=+0.01. Determine the other two nodes from the orthogonality of the cubic support polynomial to1andx under the recovered moment functional, then obtain all three weights. Verify support[-1,1], positivity and all five moments for each. ReturnP(X>=0) of the negative-node example andP(X>0) of the positive-node example. Establish that the same construction remains admissible for a sequence of nonzero middle nodes approachingzero from each side. These example values corroborate the limiting certificate; they are not substitutes for exact sharp bounds.
entropy_comparison: Among absolutely continuous laws on[-1,1] satisfying the source moments, identify the maximum DIFFERENTIAL entropyh=-integral f ln(f)dx (nats) and its maximizing law, with a global entropy argument. Return its P(X>=0). Explain whether this entropy-selected tail is point identified by the readouts when all admissible probability laws, including atoms, are allowed. Do not confuse differential entropy with Shannon entropy of a discrete extremizing law or silently restrict the uncertainty class to densities.
required_typed_evidence: Complete source-matrix SVD and moment solve; both actual moment/localizer eigenspectra and inverses; actual PolynomialRoots for the unrestricted-half-atom complementarity polynomial, bounded-half-atom interior complementarity polynomial, zero-atom quadrature support polynomial, and derivatives of both tail-bound polynomials; and actual SolveLinearSystem calls for the three extremizer weight systems. Retain all real/complex root inventories and physical domain checks. The canonical approach examples may use further typed root/linear solves or verified numerical code. Polynomial scaling and root order may vary, but complete global sign and moment feasibility must be established. All numeric execution must propagate actual source/tool observations and retain proof and residual receipts.

interpretation_proposals.A: Finite moment constraints can leave sharp distributional uncertainty even when every readout is exact.
interpretation_proposals.B: A sharp point-mass bound over the real line remains sharp after a support restriction without any additional certificate.
interpretation_proposals.C: A support-localizing constraint can be stricter than the raw moment-matrix constraint at a specified atom.
interpretation_proposals.D: Moving a boundary atom without correcting the other support/weights automatically preserves every measured moment.
interpretation_proposals.E: An atom at an event boundary can change whether a sharp probability bound is attained.
interpretation_proposals.F: A sufficiently dense finite signal grid proves the exact continuous probability extremum and its attainment status.
interpretation_proposals.G: Maximum-entropy selection and point identification from moment data are different claims.
interpretation_proposals.H: The discrete Shannon entropy of a moment extremizer is the same quantity as the maximum differential entropy on a bounded interval.

reporting: Return the public answer schema. Atom location arrays ascending with distinct atoms; weight arrays aligned and complete, positive and sum1within1e-8. Moments in powers of normalizedX, all probabilities dimensionless, entropy nats. Absolute tolerance1e-7 for numeric quantities; booleans, IDs and attainment claims exact. Probability bounds[0,1], positive atom weights and each problem support are strict scientific admissibility checks, not waived by tolerance. Report infimum/supremum values even where no extremizer exists, with their correct false attainment flag. Actual upper/lower/certificate derivations and canonical family must remain in the trajectory.

primary_context.context: Classical generalized moment problem, Gaussian quadrature and Chebyshev-Markov-Stieltjes inequalities. The controlled readout system, bounded/unrestricted atom comparison and event-boundary examples are own constructions; no external empirical data or solver ground truth are supplied.
